display.title: Episode 532: The Silver Mirror (Isru Chag Shavuos)
display.summary_short: The day after Shavuos: every Jew stood at Har Sinai and every Jew will leave exile together; then the story of a generous man whom wealth turned into a miser, and the Rebbe's lesson of the window and the mirror.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Isru Chag, the day after Shavuos 5752. Uncle Yossi recalls hearing the Ten Commandments in shul and explains that every Jewish soul of every generation stood at Har Sinai; just as not one Jew was left behind in Egypt, Moshiach will bring every single Jew back to Eretz Yisroel. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva boy recites the Shema, everyone gives tzedakah, and a sponsor message follows. Story time: Reb Avraham, a hard-working man, always welcomes the poor with an open hand. A visiting Rebbe offers him a blessing, and Reb Avraham asks for wealth so he can give more tzedakah. The Rebbe warns him that riches are a hard test. His business soon booms, but he stops davening in shul and learning, sends the poor away, and becomes a lonely miser. A year later the Rebbe returns, has him look through the window, where he sees the town's poor water carrier, woodchopper and cobbler, and then into a mirror, where he sees only himself. Both are glass, says the Rebbe, but silver coating makes you see only yourself. Reb Avraham cries, does teshuvah and becomes kinder than ever. The show ends with Tehillim chapter 20 for the Rebbe's recovery.
display.lesson: Don't let money blind you to others: use wealth to help people, and it is never too late to return to good ways.
